title: Investigate & remediate intermittent kernel misrouting causing attention 'vignetting' under mixed-length bursts
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Summary:
During a capacity ramp in dedicated pools handling mixed-length chat workloads (short system prompts + long user messages), we observed intermittent P95/P99 latency regressions and degraded token quality localized to attention-heavy models. Users reported sporadic slow tails and occasional token duplication or truncation patterns we are calling 'attention vignetting' — an emergent pattern where attention matrices are computed from an incorrect kernel path leading to effective attention window shrinkage on active subsequences.

Why this ticket exists:
This ticket captures the follow-up investigation, proposed mitigations, and implementation plan to (1) root-cause the kernel selection mismatch in the scheduler's quick-probe path, (2) stabilize KV-cache warmup interactions, and (3) deploy a safe rollback/guardrail to prevent future regressions while we iterate on a permanent fix.

Related artifacts:
- Incident notes: https://company-confluence.internal/infra/attn-vignetting-incident
- Temporal trace dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/attn-vignetting
- Repro harness and load shape: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/eng/attn-vignette-repro
timeline:
2026-02-18: First elevated alerts from dedicated-eu-3 pool (p95 spike ~2.4x)
2026-02-18: Oncall triage - initial hypothesis: batch-misalignment on mixed seq lengths
2026-02-19: Repro harness created to simulate mixed bursts; observed consistent quality degradation under high burst rate
2026-02-20: Postmortem investigation started (ENG-115001 created)
2026-02-24: Root-cause narrowed to quick-probe kernel selector backoff + stale KV cache warmup interplay
2026-03-01: Mitigation gate deployed: disable quick-probe path for models with attention split heuristics (canary on dedicated-eu-3)
2026-03-05: Canary reduced p95 regressions by ~70% but uncovered higher eviction rates in KV cache under certain schedules
2026-03-10: Decision: implement deterministic path-consistency check in scheduler and KV-cache warmup priority tuning
root_cause: A combination of (A) a probe-mode heuristic in the scheduler that would opportunistically route to a low-latency kernel variant before KV-cache priming completed, and (B) a timing window where mixed-length bursts produced partial KV cache state. The probe-mode selector underestimated attention memory pressure for long sequences, selecting a fused attention kernel optimized for shorter prefixes. That kernel's execution path effectively reduced attention receptive field for active tokens (the observed 'vignetting') and caused downstream token anomalies and tail latency as requests retried or fell back.
mitigations:
Short term (already deployed):
- Disable quick-probe routing for models with attention-tiling heuristics (canary then global) — deployed 2026-03-01.
- Temporary increase of KV-cache eviction thresholds for dedicated pools to avoid premature evictions during warmup.

Medium term (in development):
- Add scheduler path-consistency check: ensure probe route is validated against KV-cache readiness metric before committing.
- Tune probe backoff window based on sequence-length distribution sampled over the last N minutes.

Long term (Q2):
- Kernel capability tagging & compatibility matrix to make probe decisions explicit (no implicit heuristics).
- Extend eval harness to include 'vignetting' quality detectors in regression runs.

progress_updates:
2026-02-25: Repro harness validated the bug across kernels (fused-attn-short vs general-attn-long).
2026-03-01: Canary change (disable quick-probe) rolled to 10% traffic and then 100% on dedicated-eu-3; immediate tail improvement observed.
2026-03-04: Observability flagged higher KV cache residency; started tuning eviction thresholds.
2026-03-08: Design review with runtime, scheduler, and observability teams; agreed on path-consistency check approach and gating metrics.
2026-03-10: Work started on ENG-115002 and ENG-115003.
review_notes:
Design review outcomes (2026-03-08):
- Runtime: prefer conservative selectors that require affirmative KV readiness rather than heuristic assumptions.
- Scheduler: implement a synchronous validation step post-probe before committing route.
- Observability: add attention window anomaly metric and a probe-mismatch counter.
- PM: prioritize customer replay and CI coverage before full rollout.

Open questions:
- Should we implement optimistic fast-paths behind an opt-in annotation for models that have run warmup for N minutes? (Action: PM to decide by 2026-03-12)
- Can we reduce KV-cache warmup time by prefetch heuristics without increasing memory pressure? (Action: runtime team spike due 2026-03-19)
